name: ollam
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The ollam was the top rank in the Irish bardic order. Irish custom set seven levels for the Fili, the class of poets. The ollam stood at the highest step. Someone of this rank had to give all 250 chief stories of the country. The task also covered 100 of the lesser tales.

okr.objective: Define the ollam as the highest Irish bardic rank among the seven levels of Fili.
key_results: The ollam ranks above the other six bard levels.
The ollam must recite all 250 chief tales of the country.
The ollam also recites 100 lesser tales.
The title was also spelled ollamh or ollave.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore
